subject: Clarify: private deployment key custody, operator access & break-glass — AlphaMed procurement checklist
messages:
From: "AlphaMed Procurement" <procurement@alphamed.com>
To: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-08T09:12:00-08:00
Subject: Procurement checklist / private deploy – key custody questions

Hi Tessa,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement and Legal are pulling together the checklist for our private deployment (VPC + customer HSM) and have a few pinpoint questions we need to close before we can route for signature: 

1) Key custody: can Redwood operate only with a wrapped key where the private key material never leaves our HSM (customer-kept keys)? If not, what exact artifacts/remnants would be present on Redwood side (wrapped key blobs, key identifiers, attestations)?

2) Operator access: what Redwood roles, if any, can initiate a runtime decryption or access model inputs/outputs? We need a binding statement that only named operator roles with break-glass authorization (and audit trail) can do so and only under emergency conditions.

3) Subprocessors & backups: please list any subprocessors for monitoring/ops and whether backups or replicas may cross the US border (we cannot allow EU->US cross-border for PHI, and Canada backup is acceptable with advance notice).

Attached is our procurement checklist and an initial draft DPA (Legal will send redlines separately). Can you confirm the above and propose contract language we can include?

Best,
Nastasia Kaplan
Sr. Counsel, AlphaMed
procurement@alphamed.com

Attachments: AlphaMed_Procurement_Checklist.xlsx
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai

Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-08T11:03:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement checklist / private deploy – key custody questions

Nastasia — thanks for the clear list. Looping Monica (security) and Vivek (product ops) to provide the technical + contractual language. Quick answers up front so your procurement queue has something to work with: 

- We support customer-managed keys via external HSM. Runtime uses a wrapped data-encryption-key (DEK) and we never persist customer plaintext private key material.
- Redwood personnel do not have routine access to plaintext inputs/outputs. Operator access is scoped to a small set of named roles; break-glass requires 2-step authorizations (security + customer lead) and is fully audited.
- Subprocessors: monitoring/metrics and SRE partners are involved; I will include a current list and confirm cross-border backups.

Monica/Vivek — can you confirm the technical flow and propose a short DPA paragraph we can include? Nastasia, would you prefer we add explicit escrow or key-escrow refusal language?

Happy to schedule a 30-min call if that helps.

Thanks,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: monica_patel@redwood.ai
To: nastasia.kaplan@alphamed.com, procurement@alphamed.com
Cc: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-09T08:21:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement checklist / private deploy – key custody questions

Nastasia / team — technical details below, plus suggested contract language for the DPA / SOW (keeps the customer in full control of key material while allowing Redwood to operate the runtime). Attaching a simple diagram.

Technical flow (private deployment, customer-HSM model):
- Customer provisions an external HSM (FIPS-140-2/3 recommended) in their VPC.
- Customer generates and retains the KMS root key (KEK). Redwood is provisioned with a wrapped DEK: the runtime receives only the DEK encrypted with the KEK (a wrapped key blob).
- The runtime can load the wrapped-DEK into memory for the duration of the process; at no point does Redwood persist the KEK or plaintext DEK to disk. Memory is protected using our in-memory key vault with strict OS-level protections.
- All operations on model inputs/outputs happen on ephemeral runtime instances within the customer's VPC; logs containing sensitive payloads are redacted by default and only retained per agreed retention in the DPA.

Operator access & break-glass:
- Operator role model: SRE-Shift, Escalation-SRE, Customer-Partner-Engineer. Only the Escalation-SRE role has the technical capability to trigger a manual runtime snapshot and to request temporary key unwrap.
- Break-glass workflow: requires two approvals (1: Redwood security lead; 2: named AlphaMed approver) + automated ticket in our audit system. The action is time-limited (configurable TTL) and fully logged (snapshot of who/when/why).
- We will include a clause that prohibits Redwood engineers from using break-glass for any non-emergency purpose; misuse triggers immediate notification and contract remedies.

Suggested contractual language (short form):
"Customer retains exclusive control of root key material; Redwood will only operate on wrapped key blobs provided by Customer. Redwood personnel shall not access plaintext keys or customer-provided inputs/outputs except under an explicit, documented, and time-limited break-glass procedure that requires dual approval (Customer + Redwood Security). All break-glass activity shall be recorded, retained, and available to Customer upon request."

Subprocessors & backups:
- Current subprocessors that may have access to telemetry/health metrics: LogStoreCo (metrics pipeline), MetricsOps Ltd. (SRE on-call support), and CloudHealth Partners (billing). None of these subprocessors will have access to plaintext model I/O or unwrapped key material.
- Backups/replicas: by default, backups remain in the customer's configured region. We will not replicate PHI outside the region without written consent. We can accommodate Canada backup location for your use case; we will add this as a contractual restriction + notice requirement.

Attachments: kms-separation-diagram.pdf

Let me know if you want a tighter, single-sentence DPA clause or if Legal wants specific SLAs tied to break-glass response windows. Happy to iterate.

— Monica Patel
Security Architect, Redwood Inference
From: "Nastasia Kaplan" <nastasia.kaplan@alphamed.com>
To: monica_patel@redwood.ai, tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@alphamed.com, ops@alphamed.com, joe.sullivan@cloudops-consulting.com
Date: 2027-02-09T13:47:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement checklist / private deploy – key custody questions

Monica/Tessa — thanks for the thorough breakdown. A few follow-ups from Legal / CloudOps after reviewing: 

- We need explicit contractual language that "Redwood and its subprocessors shall be prohibited from training models on our data or using customer inputs/outputs to improve any models." Please confirm.
- Subprocessor list: please provide a living URL or a process for prior notice + objection for any new subprocessor that would touch telemetry/ops data.

- Break-glass: we agree the two-party approval is reasonable but request that the customer-side approver can be multiple named roles (e.g., SecurityLead, HeadOfOps) and that Redwood provides real-time notification (email + webhook) when break-glass is invoked.

- Cross-border: Canada backup is acceptable; EU replication is not. Please include the Canada location and a commitment to not replicate to EU.

I attached a redline of the DPA highlighting these asks. Also, can you confirm whether Redwood would accept (a) a clause forbidding key-escrow and (b) an audit right for AlphaMed (once yearly) to inspect audit trails and break-glass logs under NDA?

On another note: Joe from our cloud consultancy asked if we can run a 2-week pilot in a canary VPC with restricted dataset to validate the runtime and audit pipeline before we commit. We'll need a short SOW for that.

Best,
Nastasia Kaplan
Sr. Counsel, AlphaMed

Attachments: AlphaMed_DPA_Redline_v1.docx
From: tessa_morgan@redwood.ai
To: nastasia.kaplan@alphamed.com, procurement@alphamed.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.ai, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.ai, laura_bennett@redwood.ai
Date: 2027-02-10T16:44:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Procurement checklist / private deploy – key custody questions

Nastasia — appreciate the clear redlines. Confirmations + next steps below: 

1) No-training clause: Redwood will accept explicit DPA language prohibiting the use of customer-provided data for model training or model improvement. We will commit to a contractual prohibition and technical controls to enforce it. Suggested snippet to include in the DPA: 

"Provider shall not, under any circumstances, use Customer Data to train, tune, or improve any models or machine learning artifacts. Provider will implement technical safeguards to prevent Customer Data from being included in model training datasets and will attest to such controls upon Customer's request."

2) Subprocessor process: we will provide a published living list of subprocessors and a 30-day prior notice + objection process for new subprocessors that would process telemetry or logs. This will be part of the DPA appendix.

3) Break-glass & audit rights: we accept (a) multiple named approvers on Customer side, (b) real-time notification via email + webhook, and (c) an annual audit-right under NDA for audit trails / break-glass logs. We will put the audit window and evidence scope in the DPA.

4) Key-escrow refusal: Redwood will accept a clause that Redwood will not require or mandate key-escrow. If AlphaMed requests escrow, that must be handled via a separate bilateral escrow agreement (and is not required for standard private deployment).

5) Cross-border: confirm Canada backup only; no EU replication without explicit written consent. We'll enumerate permitted regions in the SOW.

6) Canary pilot SOW: we will draft a 2-week pilot SOW scoped to a restricted dataset, limited user count, and explicit acceptance criteria for audit log fidelity and break-glass test. ETA for SOW: 3 business days.

I'll send the draft DPA paragraph and SOW stub to the Drive link (SEC-901) and update the HubSpot deal. If AlphaMed legal is happy, we can aim to have a final DPA + SOW signed in the usual procurement cycle (target: end of March).

Next actions: 
- Redwood to post living subprocessor list + upload DPA paragraph (T+1 day) [SEC-901].
- Redwood to share SOW stub (T+3 business days).
- AlphaMed to review and confirm approver list and pilot schedule.

Thanks — happy to run a 30-min call if helpful.

Regards,
Tessa Morgan
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
